messages:
maria: Heads up — customer AcmeCorp is ready for private deploy onboarding next week. Need a clear handoff checklist from NetOps and an upgrade-safe network plan. They run strict egress controls and a shared NAT box.
lee: Thanks — can we confirm whether they want our agent to egress through their NAT or we should support a customer-managed egress route? That changes installer flags.
sam: They requested customer-managed egress. They have a perimeter NAT with 3 public IPs. Expecting us to provide an allowlist of destination IPs and ports.
maria: OK. Action items: 1) provide allowlist + TLS SNI expectations 2) define rollback if upgrade fails 3) staging test plan with their netops
jordan: For staging, recommend a short-lived canary that uses a dedicated tenant and IP range. If the canary's health checks pass for 30m we can roll to full tenancy. Also document our expected tcp/443 handshake and mTLS behavior.
lee: Quick draft of allowlist snippet:
```
# Allow outbound to Redwood control plane
dest: control.redwood-inference.com
ports: 443
# Long-lived websocket for streaming (same host)
protocol: TLS
```
Also we support pinning to an IP list if they can't do DNS egress.
sam: If they insist on IP-level allowlist, we need to provide a signed list (rotated monthly) and fallback domains. Operations: we'll publish via signed JSON at https://updates.redwood-inference.com/egress-ips
maria: Good. Also need to settle upgrade path: they want zero-downtime patching windows. Can Dedicated rolling updates cover this for on-prem? lee?
lee: We support node-by-node rolling upgrades for the agent and runtime. Biggest risk is persistent connections for long running streams. Plan is: drain new requests to canary, migrate sessions via short-lived handoff, keep KV cache warm. We'll document the observed latency spike pattern and expected rollback command.
jordan: Suggest we include explicit commands for their SREs in the doc, e.g.: 
```
# trigger rollback
redwoodctl rollout rollback --tenant acmecorp --version 2024-11-07
# check agent health
redwoodctl agent status --tenant acmecorp
```
maria: Perfect. Sam — can your team validate the signed IP rotation cadence (monthly) fits their compliance needs? They have quarterly audits.
sam: Monthly fine. We'll include an HMAC and release notes for each rotation. Also we'll provide a one-time onboarding script for their firewall team that outputs the iptables snippet.
lee: Minor nudge: for airgapped installs (customer asked in initial RFP) we need to add the offline bundle flow and clearly separate the network handoff steps from the package install steps in the doc.
maria: Make sense. Let's aim to have the full handoff doc and a one-page checklist ready by Friday EOD. @jordan can you own the staging test plan? @sam can you own the allowlist + signed IP publication? @lee owns rollback/runbook samples.
jordan: I can. Will include test harness (k6 + synthetic streaming) and acceptance criteria (no dropped sessions >0.5% over 30m, latency within SLO).
sam: I'll get the signed IP feed and firewall script. I'll also draft a short email template for their netops to confirm the ACLs.
lee: I'll assemble the commands and a small KB for session-migration caveats.
maria: Great — ops-bot, create a checklist task in #product-runbooks and ping the onboarding tracker.
ops-bot: Created task PROD-ONBOARD-421 in product-runbooks and set reminder for 3 days before the scheduled start. :white_check_mark:
maria: Thanks everyone. If any blocker appears, drop it here — otherwise I'll circulate the Friday draft to AcmeCorp PMs. :thumbsup:
